thread.title: Senator Ron Johnson seeks records on alleged fraud in Minnesota child care programs
thread.title_full: Senator Ron Johnson seeks records on alleged fraud in Minnesota child care programs

author: The Sconi
title: Senator Ron Johnson seeks records on alleged fraud in Minnesota child care programs
text:
U.S. Senator Ron Johnson (R-Wis.), who serves as chairman of the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, has requested records from the Minnesota Department of Human Services (DHS) regarding oversight failures and fraud detection within state-run programs. The request was made in a letter to DHS Temporary Commissioner Shireen Gandhi, with a copy sent to Governor Tim Walz.
The inquiry comes after public reports highlighted possible large-scale fraud in Minnesota’s child care assistance program and other Medicaid service categories identified by Governor Walz as “high-risk.” A YouTube video by Nick Shirley recently drew attention to an estimated $111 million in improper payments and fraud at child care centers throughout the state, raising concerns about whether current oversight practices are adequate.
“At the very least, routine DHS oversight should have identified obvious program-integrity red flags at child care centers receiving unusually large payments relative to their licensed capacity,” Chairman Johnson wrote.
In his letter, Johnson included a list of more than 70 child care businesses that received over $1 million each in annual payments from Minnesota in 2024. He called for audit and inspection records related to these entities.
“Given the pervasiveness of fraud in your state, it is past time for Minnesota to answer for its apparent failure to safeguard taxpayer dollars,” Chairman Johnson stated.
Johnson’s recent election history includes victories over Mandela Barnes in 2022, Russ Feingold in 2016, and again over Feingold in 2010.
Further details about Johnson’s letter can be found through coverage by the New York Post. The full text of his letter is also available online.
